subject: Copywriting
subcategory: The Science of Storytelling in Ads
title: Emotional Ads Outperform Rational Ones
description: A quick, practical guide to Emotional Ads Outperform Rational Ones.

hook.text: The IPA database of 1,400 ad campaigns proves that purely emotional ads are twice as profitable as purely rational ones.

buildup.text: Binet and Field analyzed 30 years of data.

discovery.text: Rational ads work for short-term activation: 'Buy now, 20% off.' Emotional ads build brand equity that compounds.

twist.text: The optimal mix is 60% emotional brand-building and 40% rational activation. Neither alone maximizes return.

climax.text: John Lewis Christmas ads in the UK invest purely in emotion. They consistently drive the highest sales of the year.

punchline.text: 60% emotion, 40% logic. The data says feel first, think second.

quiz.question: What is the optimal mix of emotional to rational advertising?

details.summary: Research by the IPA (Institute of Practitioners in Advertising) consistently shows that emotionally-driven campaigns outperform rational ones in every metric — profitability, market share growth, and long-term brand building. Emotions drive decisions; rational analysis merely justifies them...
details.whyItMatters: This is one of advertising's most robust research findings. Understanding the emotional-rational hierarchy helps brands allocate resources toward emotional storytelling rather than feature-comparison advertising.
takeaways: Emotional campaigns are roughly twice as likely to generate large profit gains
Pure emotion outperforms pure rationality, but combining both works best
Emotional advertising builds brand equity that sustains pricing power over time

faq.question: What is the IPA's evidence for emotional advertising?
faq.answer: The IPA analyzed over 1,400 creative campaigns across 30 years. Purely emotional campaigns generated roughly double the profit of purely rational campaigns. Campaigns combining both emotional and rational elements performed best, suggesting emotion should lead and reason should support.

faq.question: Why do businesses still create rational, feature-focused ads?
faq.answer: Because emotional impact is harder to measure short-term and harder to justify in boardrooms. Rational ads show immediate, attributable results.
